arxiv-2102-11270.description: Abstract The softmax policy gradient (PG) method, which performs gradient ascent under softmax policy parameterization, is arguably one of the de facto implementations of policy optimization in modern reinforcement learning. For γ \gamma -discounted infinite-horizon tabular Markov decision processes (MDPs), remarkable progress has recently been achieved towards establishing global convergence of softmax PG methods in finding a near-optimal policy.

arxiv-2108-00340.creator: Sayak Nag, Dripta S. Raychaudhuri, Sujoy Paul, and Amit K. Roy-Chowdhury
arxiv-2108-00340.description: Abstract In many applications, we are constrained to learn classifiers from very limited data (few-shot classification). The task becomes even more challenging if it is also required to identify samples from unknown categories (open-set classification). Learning a good abstraction for a class with very few samples is extremely difficult, especially under open-set settings.

pmc-10574019.title: Production of Metallic Alloy Nanowires and Particles Templated Using Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV)
pmc-10574019.creator: Sachin N Shah, Jonathan G Heddle, David J Evans, George P Lomonossoff, Rosario Pereiro
pmc-10574019.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). We demonstrate a simple, low-energy method whereby tomato mosaic virus (ToMV) particles can be used to template the production of nanowires and particles consisting of alloys of gold (Au), platinum (Pt) and palladium (Pd) in various combinations. Selective nanowire growth within the inner channel of the particles was achieved using the polymeric capping agent polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVPK30) and the reducing agent ascorbic acid.

pmc-11289451.description: This work develops a dual-layer energy management (DLEM) model for a microgrid (MG) consisting of a community, distributed energy resources (DERs), and a grid. It ensures the participation of all these energy entities of MG in the market and their interaction with each other.

pmc-11405488.title: Napping and Obesity in Adults – What do we Know?
pmc-11405488.creator: Sasiwarang Goya Wannamethee
pmc-11405488.description: Purpose of ReviewTo review the evidence on the relationship between daytime napping and obesity.Recent FindingsThere is concern that napping may be harmful to metabolic health. Prospective studies have shown long time daytime napping (> 1 h) is associated with increased diabetes risk which may be partly associated with obesity.

pmc-11531668.title: Understanding the burden of weekly somatrogon injections compared with daily somatropin injections in children with growth hormone deficiency: a plain language summary of publication
pmc-11531668.creator: Aristides K Maniatis, Mauri Carakushansky, Sonya Galcheva, Gnanagurudasan Prakasam, Larry A Fox, Adriana Dankovcikova, Jane Loftus, Andrew A Palladino, Maria de los Angeles Resa, Carrie Turich Taylor, Mehul T Dattani, Jan Lebl
pmc-11531668.description: • For children with growth hormone deficiency, once-weekly somatrogon injections were less of a burden than once-daily somatropin injections.• The safety of weekly somatrogon was similar to that of daily somatropin.• Compared with daily somatropin injections, children with growth hormone deficiency may be less likely to miss weekly somatrogon injections.

pmc-12471783.title: The Impact of Statin Use on Sepsis Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12471783.creator: Constantinos Philippou, Constantinos Tsioutis, Maria Tsiappari, Nikolaos Spernovasilis, Dimitrios Papadopoulos, Aris P. Agouridis
pmc-12471783.description: Background and Objectives: Statins are among the most prescribed medications globally, primarily due to their potent lipid-lowering capabilities. This systematic review aims to identify, synthesize and evaluate current evidence regarding the potential protective effects of statins on sepsis mortality. Materials and Methods: A thorough and comprehensive database search was conducted in PubMed and Cochrane Library until 30 January 2025.

pmc-12610322.title: Effectiveness of Vaginal Pessary Use in Improving Quality of Life Among Women with Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Prospective Study
pmc-12610322.creator: Ngoc Thi Tran, Thanh Quang Le, Hai Thanh Pham, Nam Hoang Tran, Matteo Frigerio, Yoav Baruch
pmc-12610322.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Vaginal pessaries worked with high success, improvements in quality of life, and few side effects.Most women were satisfied and felt their symptoms improved. What are the implications of the main finding? Pessaries can be used as an easy, safe first choice for women with prolapse.

pmc-13397888.creator: Wei Liang, Shuying He, Heqing Tao, Yuerong Lv, Xianjie Chen, Liang Peng
pmc-13397888.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study aimed to clarify the effect of Lactobacillus johnsonii (L. johnsonii) on immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs)-associated colitis and the efficacy of ICIs. johnsonii mitigated the severity of colitis in the experimental ICI-associated colitis model, along with a decrease in the proportions of M1 macrophages and Th1 cells and an increase in those of M2 macrophages and Tregs in the colon. johnsonii intervention upregulated the expression of tight junction proteins. johnsonii promoted tryptophan metabolism and the production of anti-inflammatory metabolites.

pmc-13474077.title: Gangrenous cholecystitis as a sentinel manifestation of chronic mesenteric ischemia in a hepatomesenteric trunk
pmc-13474077.creator: Eliana S. Suárez, Felipe Camejo, Santiago González, Luis Figoli, Marcelo Diamant
pmc-13474077.description: Chronic mesenteric ischemia is an uncommon and often underdiagnosed atherosclerotic condition due to nonspecific symptoms. The hepatomesenteric trunk is a rare anatomical variant with important clinical implications when its common origin is involved. We report the case of a 43-year-old heavy smoker presenting with progressive postprandial pain and significant weight loss.
